population.definition: Population of the agglomeration of Nouakchott comprising its three regional wilayas (Nouakchott-Nord: 614,465; Nouakchott-Ouest: 204,881; Nouakchott-Sud: 627,415) enumerated in the December 2023 General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-5) conducted by the Agence Nationale de la Statistique et de l'Analyse Démographique et Économique (ANSADE), tabulated via CityPopulation.

source.title: Mauritania: Administrative Division and Major Cities - Population Statistics (Census 2023)

facts.claim: Selected in 1957 by Moktar Ould Daddah to become the capital of independent Mauritania, Nouakchott was previously a modest fortified colonial outpost and fishing village of barely a few hundred inhabitants.

source.title: Musée National de Nouakchott: Histoire, préhistoire et traditions vivantes
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture de Mauritanie
source.quote: Fondation de la capitale moderne en 1957 sur le site d'un ancien poste colonial

facts.claim: The Port de Pêche artisanal beach wharf hosts hundreds of colorful wooden pirogues, landing hundreds of tonnes of fresh Atlantic catch daily and sustaining vital Mauritanian artisanal fishing cooperatives.

source.title: Musée National de Nouakchott: Histoire, préhistoire et traditions vivantes
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture de Mauritanie
source.quote: Le port artisanal et la plage des pêcheurs constituent le coeur battant de la vie maritime de Nouakchott

facts.claim: The National Museum of Mauritania (Musée National de Nouakchott), founded in 1972 in the Maison de la Culture, preserves Neolithic archaeological collections and nomadic Saharan ethnographic artifacts.

source.title: Musée National de Nouakchott: Histoire, préhistoire et traditions vivantes
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture de Mauritanie
source.quote: Création du Musée National en 1972 pour conserver le patrimoine préhistorique et saharien

timeline.event: Choice of Nouakchott ('Place of the Winds') as the site for the future capital of independent Mauritania, transferring government administration from Saint-Louis in Senegal.
Mauritania proclaims independence on 28 November 1960, with Nouakchott officially inaugurated as the national capital under President Moktar Ould Daddah.
Severe Sahelian droughts drive rapid sedentarization, prompting hundreds of thousands of nomadic pastoralists to settle in newly expanding districts of Nouakchott.
Reorganization of the capital district into three separate wilayas (Nouakchott-Nord, Nouakchott-Ouest, Nouakchott-Sud) across nine urban communes.
